Per this card's own ordering clause — "until the member is out of the vendored spec, removing the designer entries would desync the designer from the still-declared vocabulary" — starting now would remove designer support for a location the consumed contract still declares, the half-state the clause forbids (and objectui's declaration-parity gates judge against the resolved install, so the desync would likely also be a red gate, not just a principle).

**New blocking condition: the next `@objectstack/spec` release (> rc.5) reaching objectui's resolved install.** That is the same single event gating #6955 — so one spec publish unlocks the final two `target:v17` objectui-half cards at once. This seat re-checks the npm dist-tag each patrol round and dispatches immediately when it moves; no further action needed from anyone until then, except the release itself (maintainer's action, already flagged on the seat report).

Session `session_01RnQd8iMMUwXQEV1crFmQiQ`, branch `claude/issue-7100-global-nav-designer` (never created — nothing to implement).

## What landed, and when

PR **objectui#4169** — *"retire(studio): drop the global_nav designer surfaces with the rc.6 spec bump (objectstack#7100)"* — was **merged 2026-08-11T03:30:29Z** by `yinlianghui`. Its changeset was then consumed by the release `chore: release packages (#4126)` (main `5bf5d2cb6`, 2026-08-14T08:20Z), publishing the retirement as **17.5.0**.

The card's ordering clause was satisfied by that PR coupling the removals to the rc.6 bump in one commit, exactly as the clause required.

## Measured on post-merge `origin/main` (`2165d889a`, includes today's #4657/#4660/#4651)

All four scope sites are retired, each with a tombstone comment naming the ruling:

| Card site (as written) | Actual path | State on `main` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ActionPreview.tsx` mock palette frame | `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/ActionPreview.tsx:581` | frame gone; tombstone comment in its place |
| `ActionDefaultInspector.tsx` entry | `.../inspectors/ActionDefaultInspector.tsx:123` | `LOCATION_LABELS` is exactly the 6 live members |
| `block-config.ts` palette option | `.../previews/block-config.ts:479` | option list is exactly the 6 live members |
| `action-bar.tsx` doc comment | `packages/components/src/renderers/action/action-bar.tsx:20` | aligned; notes the enum is `[...ACTION_LOCATIONS]` and followed on its own |

Also already done beyond the card's letter: the orphaned `engine.inspector.pageBlock.option.location.global_nav` key is gone from **both** locale tables (`i18n.ts:679` en, `:2429` zh), and regression pins exist — `previews/__tests__/ActionPreview.locations.test.tsx` (negative pins beside positive ones over the same render) and a new block in `previews/__tests__/block-config.test.ts`.

A full sweep of `origin/main` for `global_nav` outside CHANGELOGs returns **no live authoring surface** — only tombstone comments, those pin tests, and `react/src/hooks/__tests__/useActionEngine.test.ts`, which deliberately keeps a `@ts-expect-error` fixture to pin that the schema rejects the value (`ActionLocationSchema.safeParse('global_nav')`).

## Two corrections to the dispatch prompt

1. **`packages/metadata-admin` does not exist in objectui.** No workspace package by that name exists anywhere in the repo. All of this card's files live in `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/`, i.e. package **`@object-ui/app-shell`**. This matters for the disjointness argument in the claim comment: `PackageFormDialog.tsx` (the objectstack#8270 continuation) is at `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PackageFormDialog.tsx` — the **same package and the same directory**, not "a different package". The two file sets are still disjoint, so there was no real conflict, but the reasoning that established it was based on a package that isn't there.
2. Earlier state on this card is stale: the 2026-08-10 review comment says *"PR #4169 stays DRAFT until #4165 is ruled"*. It did not — it was merged the next morning. The 2026-08-14 unlock sweep and dispatch both read the card as unstarted, and neither re-checked the PR.

## Deliberately NOT filed as a finding

`ROADMAP.md:1369` still lists `global_nav` among the locations `action:bar` filters by. That is **a documented decision, not drift**: it sits under the dated, completed milestone heading `### P2.10 ActionBar Rendering & useActionEngine Integration ✅` (a historical record, not a live contract statement), and PR #4169's body called it out explicitly *"so it reads as a decision, not an oversight."* Filing it would re-litigate a settled call.

## Verification scope, stated honestly

No worktree, no install, no build, no test run — there is nothing to verify a change against, and re-running a 14.6k-test suite over code merged three days ago and released since would spend shared-container budget for no new information. The evidence above is direct `git grep`/blob reads against `origin/main` plus the merged-PR and release records. PR #4169's own body records its verification at merge time: `turbo run build` 44/44, `vitest run` 14,609/14,615, and a reverse verification that went red-on-restore (4 failed / 19 passed) proving the pins are not vacuous.

**Recommended PM action:** close this card as completed against objectui#4169 / `@object-ui/app-shell` 17.5.0, and drop it from the `target:v17` board — the v17 obligation it tracked is discharged.
